competitive_landscape: Jadrolinija (state operator) and Kapetan Luka (Krilo) run dense diesel catamaran service today — clear demand proof — plus the largest charter-fleet base in the Adriatic via the ACI marina network. Service is weather-limited and emissions-heavy; the protected channels and short legs are an ideal all-electric foiling fit. No zero-emission foiling operator runs the Dalmatian chain.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II owns the entire central-Dalmatian lattice — Brač (~12 nm), Šolta (~14 nm), Hvar (~23 nm), Vis (~30 nm), Hvar↔Korčula (~22 nm) — all inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope on sheltered channels.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) runs the long coastal trunk Split↔Dubrovnik (~100 nm) and Split↔Zadar without island charging dependency.

precedents.why_it_matters: Dalmatia is the European twin of a dense protected island chain served from one gateway hub.
Demonstrates demand for premium all-electric island-hopping at scale — directly transferable to the Adriatic charter base.

regulatory_note: Croatian flag / EU regime; Croatian Ministry of the Sea, Transport and Infrastructure + harbour-master offices; ACI (state marina chain) is the dominant berthing concessionaire. EU maritime decarbonization (FuelEU Maritime) and growing local pressure on diesel-ferry emissions in protected waters create a regulatory tailwind for zero-emission craft.
seasonality: Strong Apr–Oct, peak Jun–Sep; the sheltered channels extend the shoulder season versus open-sea routes. Winter island-commuter demand persists for the inhabited islands (Brač, Hvar, Korčula, Vis), giving a year-round public-transport base under the seasonal tourism peak.

summary: Central Dalmatia is, by geography, one of the best island-hopping markets on earth: a dense lattice of inhabited islands — Brač, Hvar, Vis, Šolta, Korčula — strung along sheltered channels just short hops apart, anchored by Split's UNESCO old town and its busy passenger port. Croatia ran 226 nautical-tourism ports including 85 marinas in 2024 and ranks among the world's top yachting destinations; charter fleets out of Split, Trogir and the ACI marina network are the backbone of the Adriatic season. Conventional Jadrolinija and Krilo catamarans already prove dense daily demand, but they are diesel and weather-limited; every core Dalmatian leg sits comfortably inside the 70 nm Pioneer II envelope, and the protected channels mean calm, reliable, year-shoulder operation. This is the European twin of the SEA and Maldives island-hop cases.
tagline: The densest protected island chain in the Mediterranean — Split is the gateway to Brač, Hvar, Vis and Korčula, every hop inside Pioneer II range.
